title: Time-Weighted Vector Retrieval
summary: Blend semantic relevance with task-appropriate freshness while distinguishing publication time, event time, and validity.
overview: Time-weighted retrieval adjusts evidence ranking using temporal information. A recent incident update may matter more than an older operational note, while a foundational specification may remain authoritative for years. The correct time signal depends on the question: publication date, last modification, event occurrence, and effective validity are not interchangeable.

A common architecture combines a relevance score with a calibrated freshness function after applying hard validity constraints. Freshness is a preference; superseded or not-yet-effective policy status is often an eligibility rule. Time decay should be tuned by document class and query intent rather than applied uniformly to the entire corpus.

production.poc: A prototype compares relevance-only results with time-aware ranking on explicitly time-sensitive questions.
production.production: Production normalizes timestamps, preserves source timezone and validity, and distinguishes live status from historical queries.
production.scale: At scale, handle late-arriving events, clock errors, source-specific freshness contracts, and evaluation across both current and historical evidence needs.

components.name: Temporal metadata parser
components.role: Extracts publication, event, modification, and effective dates with provenance.

components.name: Query time resolver
components.role: Determines whether the user asks about now, a historical point, or a period.

components.name: Eligibility filter
components.role: Excludes evidence outside required validity or authorization constraints.

components.name: Ranking combiner
components.role: Balances semantic relevance and document-class-specific recency.

components.name: Freshness monitor
components.role: Detects delayed ingestion and source update gaps.

flow.title: Resolve temporal intent
flow.description: Identify the requested reference time and clarify internally whether current or historical evidence is needed.

flow.title: Filter validity
flow.description: Exclude superseded or future-effective records where the task requires active guidance.

flow.title: Retrieve semantically
flow.description: Collect relevant candidates without allowing recency to substitute for topic relevance.

flow.title: Apply time weighting
flow.description: Use the appropriate timestamp and calibrated decay for each evidence class.

flow.title: Check conflicting revisions
flow.description: Prefer authoritative active versions while retaining historical context when requested.

flow.title: Expose freshness
flow.description: Attach source dates and any ingestion lag to the answer’s evidence.

useCase.title: Summarizing an evolving incident
useCase.situation: An incident assistant summarizes an active service compromise from investigation notes and status updates.
useCase.problem: An older high-similarity note describes a hypothesis that later evidence disproved.
useCase.requirement: Favor current supported findings while retaining the timeline of changed understanding.
useCase.architecture: Incident documents carry event time, publication time, and supersession links.
runtime: The query asks for current containment status.
The retriever prioritizes the latest authoritative status while linking earlier hypotheses as historical context.
useCase.failure: A late-arriving note with an old event timestamp does not automatically replace newer operational status.
useCase.impact: Track stale-evidence selections, source lag, and historical-query accuracy; freshness improvements should not erase useful older evidence.

tradeoffs.cost: Requires reliable version and effective-date metadata.

failures.detection: One record ranks first across unrelated current queries.
failures.recovery: Validate timestamp bounds and quarantine implausible metadata.

failures.detection: Query time is ignored by the filter.
failures.recovery: Carry an explicit reference time through retrieval and generation.

mistakes.mistake: Using file modification as event time
mistakes.fix: Store the different temporal meanings separately.

mistakes.mistake: Applying one decay rate to every source
mistakes.fix: Calibrate by document class and task.
Preserve source authority and validity rules.

whenToUse: Use for incidents, news, inventory, and changing policies.
Use when users ask time-qualified questions.
Use when stale evidence is a measured failure mode.
whenNotToUse: Avoid aggressive decay for stable technical standards.
Do not infer freshness from missing timestamps.
Avoid recency weighting as a replacement for version control.
checklist: Test historical as well as current queries.
